verdict.rationale: Built-in virtualization is a fair axis for an operating system, but the evidence pack never documents Windows itself running a full Windows environment in a VM. The only VM mention describes a user running Windows as a guest under Linux, which is a user-side arrangement on another host platform, not a capability Windows provides. The WSL mention concerns Linux userland on Windows, which is a different capability.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run a full Windows environment in a virtual machine for apps not natively available
